title: Microsoft Teams: identify external bots joining meetings
summary: The briefing passes: its policy paths, commands, default and licensing statements are supported. It accurately reports the rollout notice and distinguishes Microsoft's inconsistent PowerShell examples from the documented meeting-policy controls.

claims.claim: The change concerns identifying external bots joining Microsoft Teams meetings.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams: Identify bots joining your Teams meetings

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap status is Rolling out.
claims.quote: "status": "Rolling out", "statusKey": "rolling-out"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap target is May CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "May CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Targeted Release.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Targeted Release"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant) and GCC.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Android, Desktop, iOS and Mac.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Android", "Desktop", "iOS", "Mac"]

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-05-19T22:45:25.
The roadmap describes a clear representation of external bots while they wait in the lobby.
claims.quote: organizers will be able to see a clear representation of the bots while they wait in the lobby.

claims.claim: The roadmap calls for organisers to explicitly and separately admit bots only if really required.
claims.quote: Organizers will be required to explicitly and separately admit these bots into the meeting, if really required.

claims.claim: Teams detects external meeting bots, including transcription or note-taking tools, attempting to join meetings hosted by the organisation.
claims.quote: External meeting assistant tools (such as transcription or note-taking bots) are increasingly used in meetings. ... Microsoft Teams provides admins with controls to detect and manage external bots when they attempt to join meetings hosted in their organization.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Bot detection is on by default and reaches organisers without administrator action.
claims.quote: Bot detection will be enabled by default for all tenants.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The default bot policy requires explicit approval before detected bots join.
claims.quote: When detected, require approval before joining (default) | RequireApprovalWhenDetected | Detected external bots are placed in the meeting lobby and require explicit approval before joining.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The bot control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting join & lobby > Manage external bots and their access to meetings.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Meetings > Meeting policies. Select the policy you want to modify, or create a new policy. Under Meeting join & lobby, find Manage external bots and their access to meetings.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ExternalBotAccessMode RequireApprovalWhenDetected sets the specified policy to require bot approval.
claims.quote: RequireApprovalWhenDetected: When detected, bots will be enforced to the meeting lobby, regardless of the lobby setting of the meeting. They will require approval before getting access to the meetings. This is the default value.

claims.claim: The lobby admission control is at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Meeting join & lobby > Who can admit from lobby.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, expand Meetings and then select Meeting policies. Select the policy that you want to update. In the Meeting join & lobby sections, update the settings that you want to change: ... Who can admit from lobby

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -UsersCanAdmitFromLobby OrganizerAndCoOrganizersOnly sets the lobby-admission default to organisers and co-organisers.
claims.quote: To control who can admit users from the lobby, use the -UsersCanAdmitFromLobby parameter. ... Only allow organizers and co-organizers to admit participants from the lobby ... OrganizerAndCoOrganizersOnly

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: The bot setting applies to meetings hosted by users assigned the meeting policy.
claims.quote: The setting applies to meetings hosted by users assigned the meeting policy.

claims.claim: Learn documents three policy choices: Do not detect bots, When detected, require approval before joining, and Block all detected bots.
claims.quote: Do not detect bots | AllowBots ... When detected, require approval before joining (default) | RequireApprovalWhenDetected ... Block all detected bots | BlockDetectedBots

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: With approval required, detected bots wait in the lobby regardless of the meeting's lobby configuration.
claims.quote: When detected, require approval before joining: Detected bots are placed in the meeting lobby regardless of the meeting's lobby configuration.

claims.claim: Registered bots appear in the lobby's Waiting section.
claims.quote: In the meeting lobby, registered bots appear in the Waiting section

claims.claim: Unverified bots detected by Teams appear under Suspected threats.
claims.quote: unverified bots detected through behavioral and infrastructure signals appear under Suspected threats.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Some bots escape detection and can continue joining according to existing meeting access settings.
claims.quote: Some bots may not be detected and may continue to join meetings according to existing meeting access settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Bot detection can incorrectly flag a human participant.
claims.quote: Detection may incorrectly identify a human participant as a bot.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: External meeting bots can record or transcribe meetings.
claims.quote: These bots may: Record or transcribe meetings without participant awareness.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: External meeting bots can store meeting content in third-party systems outside the organisation's compliance boundaries.
claims.quote: Store meeting data in third-party systems outside of the organization's compliance boundaries.

claims.claim: Do not detect bots disables detection and marking of bots in the lobby and meeting.
claims.quote: Bots aren't detected or marked in the lobby or in the meeting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Why it matters
claims.claim: Bots not detected are treated as external participants subject to existing access and lobby settings, including anonymous-join controls where applicable.
claims.quote: They appear as any other external participant in the meetings and follow the meeting's existing access and lobby settings.

claims.claim: Block all detected bots automatically blocks detected bots without an organiser admission decision.
claims.quote: Block all detected bots: Detected bots are automatically blocked from joining the meeting. They aren't placed in the meeting lobby for organizer approval

claims.claim: The blocking policy does not guarantee that all external bots are blocked.
claims.quote: The Block all detected bots option applies to bots identified by Teams detection mechanisms. It does not guarantee that all external bots will be blocked.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A participant incorrectly identified as a bot may be prevented from joining under Block all detected bots.
claims.quote: Block all detected bots: Participants incorrectly identified as bots may be prevented from joining the meeting.

claims.claim: Where supported, eligible incorrectly detected participants can use email verification recovery to verify their identity and attempt to join.
claims.quote: Where supported, eligible participants can use the email verification recovery experience to verify their identity and attempt to join.

claims.claim: Organisers, and presenters depending on the meeting setting, can explicitly admit detected bots under the approval policy.
claims.quote: Organizers (also presenters, depending on the meeting setting), need to explicitly admit these bots into the meeting.

claims.claim: Learn recommends configuring lobby admission for organisers and co-organisers only when bot approval is required.
claims.quote: If you use the Require approval before joining option, configure meeting lobby settings so that only organizers and co-organizers can admit participants.

claims.claim: The lobby page gives Organizers and presenters as the Who can admit from lobby default.
claims.quote: By default, the Who can admit from lobby policy is set to Organizers and presenters

claims.claim: The lobby admission policy sets a default rather than an enforced value because organisers can change it in Meeting options.
claims.quote: This policy sets a default that your organizers can change through their Meeting options.

claims.claim: MC1251206 says detection analyses meeting join metadata to identify external automated bots.
claims.quote: This change introduces detection logic that analyzes meeting join metadata to identify external automated bots attempting to join meetings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Organisers can use This is not a bot in the lobby to correct an incorrectly detected participant's representation in that meeting.
claims.quote: Organizers can admit the participant from the lobby and use the This is not a bot option to correct the participant's representation in that meeting.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn asks users to report undetected external bots through the Feedback option in Teams.
claims.quote: Help improve the system by reporting any undetected external meeting bots to us via the Feedback option in Teams.

claims.claim: The included licensing model reflects a new option within Teams under the product's general Teams licence requirement.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Each organisational user needs a Teams licence to use Teams except for joining meetings anonymously.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence specific to bot detection as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external bot detection license pricing meter Teams Premium; read manage-external-bots and user-access; searched licensing-enhance-teams for bot/detect. No bot-detection licence requirement found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a meter specific to bot detection as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams external bot detection license pricing meter Teams Premium; read manage-external-bots and user-access; searched licensing-enhance-teams for bot/meter/pay-as-you-go. No bot-detection meter found; MC1251206 also names none.

claims.claim: MC1251206 says all organisations using Teams meetings are affected, including GCC tenants.
claims.quote: All organizations using Microsoft Teams meetings, including GCC tenants

claims.claim: Learn describes the bot option as a meeting policy scoped at user or group level.
claims.quote: Scope: Meetings policies at a user / group level

claims.claim: The bot option can be configured in the default org-wide policy or in a targeted policy.
claims.quote: Configure this meeting policy at the tenant level with the default org-wide meeting policy or configure for a specific user group/user by creating or modifying the appropriate targeted meeting policy.

claims.claim: MC1251206 says the change cannot be controlled through Entra ID group membership at this time.
claims.quote: It cannot be controlled through Entra ID group membership at this time.

claims.claim: The bot feature's Learn applicability banner marks Meetings as applicable and Events as not applicable.
claims.quote: APPLIES TO: Image of a checkmark for yes Meetings Image of a x for no Events

claims.claim: MC1251206 lists two bot-policy options, do not detect bots and require approval, unlike Learn's three-option list.
claims.quote: A new meeting policy will be available in the Teams admin center that allows admins to configure how detected bots are handled (do not detect bots, require approval).

claims.claim: MC1251206 was updated on 22 September 2026.
claims.quote: Updated September 22, 2026: We have updated the timeline.

claims.claim: MC1251206 gives Targeted Release from mid-May 2026 to early June 2026.
claims.quote: Targeted Release: We will begin rolling out in mid-May 2026 and expect to complete by early June 2026.

claims.claim: MC1251206 gives Worldwide General Availability rollout from early June 2026 to the end of October 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early June 2026 and expect to complete by end of October 2026 (previously mid-September).

claims.claim: MC1251206 gives GCC General Availability rollout from early June 2026 to the end of October 2026.
claims.quote: General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out in early June 2026 and expect to complete by end of October 2026 (previously mid-September).

claims.claim: MC1251206 identifies mid-September as the previous General Availability completion target.
claims.quote: expect to complete by end of October 2026 (previously mid-September)

claims.claim: Microsoft's end date for MC1251206 is 30 November 2026.
claims.quote: Published 2026-03-13; last updated 2026-09-22; Microsoft's end date 2026-11-30

claims.claim: MC1251206 sets no act-by date.
claims.quote: Act by: none

claims.claim: MC1251206 says no action is required at this time.
claims.quote: No action is required at this time.

claims.claim: Learn advises testing blocking with a selected group before organisation-wide application.
claims.quote: Consider testing the blocking policy with a selected group of users before applying it organization-wide.

claims.claim: Learn gives Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" | Select-Object Identity, ExternalBotAccessMode to view the configured setting.
claims.quote: To view the configured policy setting: Get-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" | Select-Object Identity, ExternalBotAccessMode

claims.claim: MC1251206 says Microsoft intends to provide expanded administrative controls.
claims.quote: In the future, we intend to provide more granular controls to admins, as appropriate.

claims.claim: The bot feature page's PowerShell example blocks print Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy for ExternalBotAccessMode.
claims.quote: Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity "<policy name>" -ExternalBotAccessMode RequireApprovalWhenDetected

claims.claim: The bot feature page's explanatory text names Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy for ExternalBotAccessMode, matching the cmdlet reference rather than its examples.
claims.quote: You can use the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy PowerShell cmdlet to manage this policy option. You need to set the "ExternalBotAccessMode" attribute.

claims.claim: The feature page gives AllowBots and BlockDetectedBots while the cmdlet reference gives AllowAllBots for disabling detection.
claims.quote: AllowAllBots: Don't detect bots; Bots will appear the same as other participants. Standard lobby policies will apply to them.

claims.claim: The lobby page's example for organiser/co-organiser admission pairs the value with AutoAdmittedUsers rather than the UsersCanAdmitFromLobby parameter its text names.
claims.quote: To control who can admit users from the lobby, use the -UsersCanAdmitFromLobby parameter. ... Set-CsTeamsEventsPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AutoAdmittedUsers OrganizerAndCoOrganizersOnly

claims.claim: Learn recommends audit-log monitoring for unusual participant activity.
claims.quote: Monitor audit logs for unusual participant activity.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Organisers may see new bot indicators and approval prompts.
claims.quote: Inform meeting organizers that they may see new indicators and approval prompts when detected bots attempt to join meetings.
